clue.text: Attractive ribbon put to sound use

definitions.text: Attractive ribbon put to sound use

parts.words: Attractive ribbon put to sound use
parts.note: a strip that attracts in the physical sense, a magnet's pull, used for recording audio

explanation.surface: A pretty ribbon finds a musical purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attractive' reads as pretty but means drawing iron to it, and the 'ribbon' is a recording strip; 'sound use' means storing audio.
explanation.definitionFit: Recording strips coated with iron oxide store audio on a reel, a ribbon used for sound.

clue.text: Country doctor, a fabulous old bird, joining the company

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A rural GP, a legendary bird and a business all join together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country doctor' looks like one phrase, but 'Country' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a kingdom of North Africa, a nation state.

clue.text: Making points in class can have a devastating effect

indicators.note: the compass points sit inside the word for class

parts.note: a grade is a class or rank
E and N are compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: Scoring points in a lesson can have huge impact.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'can' is slang for a bomb or grenade, so the definition says the can has a devastating effect. 'Making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-thrown bomb is built to explode, and slang calls such a canister a can.

clue.text: Judges may find a'time's set

indicators.note: what the letters may find is a new arrangement, the setter's loose signal to reorder them

explanation.surface: Referees discover that a period has been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A TIME'S SET are rearranged; 'Judges' is a verb, as in reckons a value.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a figure roughly is to reckon or guess it, a verb sense.

clue.text: One's allowed to see this little place

parts.note: one is: I (one) plus S for 'is'
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Someone is given permission to visit a small spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as I'S, one is; 'to see this' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island is a tiny spot of land, a little place surrounded by water.

clue.text: Worry about raising golden blossom

indicators.note: the word for worry goes around the other piece

parts.note: to tease is to worry or pester

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Fretting over growing a yellow flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns OR into RO, and 'about' puts TEASE around it: TEA(RO)SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea rose is a hybrid flower, so it is a bloom.

clue.text: A worker falling in a heap on thereof

indicators.note: the insect drops inside the word for heap

parts.note: a pile is a heap
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer tumbles into a pile on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thereof' is 'the roof' run together in the printed text; the definition is a thing found on the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantile is a curved roofing tile, so it sits up on the top of a house.

clue.text: Speed check

parts.note: not a radar trap but simply a slowing down, a check to speed

explanation.surface: A police radar measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: Slowing down is the reduction of velocity, which checks how fast one goes.

clue.text: Intent on Eastern development

indicators.note: the word develops into a new form, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Focused on progress in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious and determined describes someone intent on a goal.

clue.text: He's not yet qualified as a sovereign employee

parts.note: a sovereign is a pound coin, and L stands for pound (libra)
an earner is one who works for wages

explanation.surface: A trainee working for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests a monarch but is the gold pound coin, giving L.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee, such as a driver with L plates, has not yet passed the test.

clue.text: The recording is not right nor is it great

indicators.note: the letters are not in the right order and must be reordered

explanation.surface: The recording is mediocre, neither accurate nor impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' reads as a judgement on the recording but is the signal to rearrange NOR IS IT GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Entering something in an official register is recording it.

clue.text: Shout, but no longer make demands

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
to claim is to demand as a right

explanation.surface: Yell, but stop insisting.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out suddenly is to call out loudly.

clue.text: The sound of traffic in a metropolitan area?

explanation.surface: Car horns in a city district.
explanation.walkthrough: Tooting is a district of south London, so the horn noise is also a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: Car horns hoot as traffic, and a South London suburb has the same name.

clue.text: To call up about a woman is all right

indicators.note: the woman's name goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: Eve is a woman's name
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Phoning a woman is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon up a memory or feeling is to bring it to mind.

clue.text: Awful scare lest solution can't be found

indicators.note: awful letters are in a mess, signalling they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A frightening worry that no answer exists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' is a link here: the solution is something that cannot be found.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving no sign behind means something cannot be tracked down.

clue.text: Article on church or island personage providing a link

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
taken as written
the Isle of Man is an island

explanation.surface: An item about church or island figures who connect people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a down-clue link: AN sits on top of CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A TV presenter links the parts of a broadcast, and a relay's last runner anchors the team.

clue.text: Painstaking preparation

parts.note: read as pain-taking: a medicine prepared to take away pain

explanation.surface: Careful groundwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painstaking' means careful, but read as 'pain-taking' it is a remedy that takes pain away.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller is a drug preparation that removes pain.

clue.text: A man putting on a quiet and industrious guy

parts.note: p is piano, quiet in music
a plier is one who plies, works steadily

explanation.surface: A man dressing a silent, hard-working fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'A' belongs to the definition; the second 'a' gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: One who applies something puts it on, as paint to a wall.

clue.text: The rifle range

parts.note: not a shooting range but the distance a gun can reach

explanation.surface: A place for target practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Within a shot's carry means the distance a firearm can reach.

clue.text: Music man given spot by royal characters

parts.note: a pip is a spot, as on dice or cards
ER, Elizabeth Regina, are royal initials

explanation.surface: A musician spotted by royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the pipes is a musician.

clue.text: Dives has bungled charge in addition

annotationWithheld.why: Dives has bungled charge in addition: PS (in addition) around LUNGE (charge) gives PLUNGES, but 'bungled' has no job; the clue as held looks misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Dives has bungled charge in addition

clue.text: It may be so steep she'll write

indicators.note: it may be another arrangement of the letters, the setter's loose signal to reorder

explanation.surface: A climb so steep that a woman will write about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A female poet is a woman who writes verse.

clue.text: Threatens to finish in bad spirits

indicators.note: the word for finish goes inside the spirits

parts.note: imps are mischievous little devils
end means finish

explanation.surface: Menaces to end things among the mischief-makers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something looming or about to happen threatens, hangs over us.

clue.text: Youngster bearing with a prude

parts.note: S, south, is a compass bearing
a prig is a prude

explanation.surface: A young person carrying a priggish companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is an old word for a young man, a stripling.

clue.text: Love turning up some time before Easter loaded with cash

parts.note: O is love, nil in tennis

indicators.note: the little word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Lent is the forty days before Easter

explanation.surface: Love blossoms before Easter for someone rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy and affluent describes someone rich, slang loaded.

clue.text: Not one can get in there

indicators.note: the letters can get into a new order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: No one is able to enter that place.
explanation.definitionFit: Not either of two, so not one or the other.

clue.text: Making many a turn round catch will generate a current

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, a large number

indicators.note: the turn goes around the catch

parts.note: a go is a turn
a net is a catch, as of fish

explanation.surface: Many a round of spinning will produce electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' is a link; 'round' puts GO around NET to give GNETO.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical generator with permanent magnets produces current, as in ignition systems.

clue.text: Leading players sprang to it so excitedly

indicators.note: the letters jump about excitedly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The stars leapt to the task eagerly.
explanation.definitionFit: Main characters in a drama are the leading figures.
